description: Add the human-in-the-loop approval mechanism and wire it in: a WriteApprovalHook (BeforeToolCallEvent interrupt) in a new agent/approval.py, register it + the FEAT-001 write tools in agent/strands_agent.py, and add the interrupt/approve-loop driver (+ [SYSTEM] signal emission) to agent/chat.py. Depends on FEAT-001 (needs the write tools + their names). The HITL mechanism is decided in task2-hitl-decision.md (native Strands interrupt) and detailed in task2-design.md; implement it faithfully. No change to agent/prompts.py. Completing this feature makes a write request produce a PROPOSAL (no HTTP write) and only execute the POST/PUT after an explicit approve, with the branch->commit->PR [SYSTEM] breadcrumbs.
steps: READ FIRST: docs/.agents/tasks/task2-hitl-writes/context.json, this file, and FEAT-001's findings, then the 'The HITL flow', 'Chaining and the [SYSTEM] signal', 'REPL / approval driver', and 'Module layout and wiring' sections of docs/.agents/tasks/task2-design.md and all of task2-hitl-decision.md. context.json replaces re-exploration.

Create agent/approval.py. Imports: from strands.hooks import BeforeToolCallEvent, HookProvider, HookRegistry. Define WRITE_TOOL_NAMES: set[str] = {the six tool names: jira_create_story, jira_update_story, github_create_branch, github_commit_files, github_open_pull_request, servicenow_create_incident}. Define build_proposal(tool_use) -> dict returning {'action','system','params','description'}: derive action from the tool name (strip the service prefix, e.g. github_create_branch -> 'create_branch'), system from the prefix ('jira'/'github'/'servicenow'), params = dict(tool_use['input']), description = a human sentence per the design examples (e.g. "Create branch '{branch_name}' in {repo_id} from {from_branch}"). Define class WriteApprovalHook(HookProvider) with register_hooks(self, registry, **kwargs): registry.add_callback(BeforeToolCallEvent, self._before_tool_call). _before_tool_call(event): name = event.tool_use['name']; if name not in WRITE_TOOL_NAMES: return (no-op, reads pass through); else response = event.interrupt('write_approval', reason=build_proposal(event.tool_use)) (first pass raises InterruptException and stops the loop; on resume returns the stored response); if response != 'APPROVE': event.cancel_tool = 'Write rejected by user.'

Wire into agent/strands_agent.py: add imports of JIRA_WRITE_TOOLS/GITHUB_WRITE_TOOLS/SERVICENOW_WRITE_TOOLS and WriteApprovalHook; add module-level WRITE_TOOLS = [*JIRA_WRITE_TOOLS, *GITHUB_WRITE_TOOLS, *SERVICENOW_WRITE_TOOLS]; in build_agent() change the final return to Agent(model=model, tools=[*READ_TOOLS, *WRITE_TOOLS], system_prompt=system_prompt, hooks=[WriteApprovalHook()]). Leave the BedrockModel construction and prompt assembly exactly as-is (stays lazy/offline-safe).

Add the approval driver to agent/chat.py: replace _ask(agent, message) so it calls result = agent(message) then while getattr(result, 'stop_reason', None) == 'interrupt': for each itr in result.interrupts capture proposal = itr.reason, print(f'\nPROPOSED: {proposal["description"]}'), read input('Approve this write? [y/N] '), decision = 'APPROVE' if yes else 'REJECT', collect approved proposals and the [{'interruptResponse': {'interruptId': itr.id, 'response': decision}}] responses; result = agent(responses); for each approved proposal call _emit_system_signal(agent, proposal). Return str(result).strip(). Implement _emit_system_signal(agent, proposal) switching on proposal['action'] using the THREE verbatim templates from task2-design.md (create_branch / commit_files / open_pull_request, substituting proposal['params'] keys repo_id/branch_name/branch/head/base) and the generic fallback "[SYSTEM] The user approved and the '{action}' action was executed." for the other writes; append one assistant-role {'role':'assistant','content':[{'text': msg}]} message to agent.messages. Emit on APPROVE only; nothing on reject. Keep _run_single and _run_repl using the same _ask.

Extend agent/tests/test_write_tools_unit.py (created in FEAT-001) with the HOOK and DRIVER tests. HOOK propose path: a tiny fake BeforeToolCallEvent exposing .tool_use and an interrupt(name, reason=None, response=None) that raises InterruptException on the first (unanswered) call; assert hook._before_tool_call propagates InterruptException for each write tool name and that build_proposal produced the right {action,system,params,description}; assert a non-write name is a no-op (no interrupt raised); assert no POST/PUT occurs on the propose path (make_request spy records zero write calls). HOOK reject path: fake event whose interrupt() returns 'REJECT'; assert the hook sets event.cancel_tool to 'Write rejected by user.' and runs no body. DRIVER: a fake agent whose __call__ returns an object with stop_reason=='interrupt' and .interrupts (each with .id and .reason proposal dict) on the first call, then a normal result; assert _ask builds the interruptResponse with the correct interruptId, re-invokes, and appends the [SYSTEM] signal into agent.messages on approve (monkeypatch builtins.input) and appends nothing on reject.
acceptance_criteria: agent/approval.py imports cleanly and exposes the three symbols: `& "<venv-py>" -c "from agent.approval import WriteApprovalHook, WRITE_TOOL_NAMES, build_proposal; assert len(WRITE_TOOL_NAMES)==6; print('approval OK')"` prints approval OK.

build_agent() registers 19 read + 6 write tools and the hook with no network/creds: `& "<venv-py>" -c "from agent.strands_agent import build_agent, READ_TOOLS, WRITE_TOOLS; build_agent(); print('read',len(READ_TOOLS),'write',len(WRITE_TOOLS))"` prints read 19 write 6.
agent/chat.py imports cleanly and _ask detects stop_reason=='interrupt', resumes with the correct interruptId, and appends a [SYSTEM] message to agent.messages only on approve.
The hook propose-path tests show InterruptException raised and ZERO HTTP write calls; the reject-path test shows event.cancel_tool set and no body run.
agent/prompts.py is unchanged; the full suite passes: existing Task 1 unit tests + all new write/hook/driver tests green, live integration test SKIPS (tunnel down).
